subject: general
question: Bholanath Singh was the leader of which of the following revolts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamar Revolt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bholanath Singh** was a key leader of the **Tamar Revolt**, which took place in the late 18th century and early 19th century.
 
• The Tamar Revolt was primarily led by the **tribal communities** in the Chotanagpur region, located in present-day Jharkhand.
 
• The revolt was triggered by the imposition of oppressive taxes and exploitation by the British East India Company and local landlords (zamindars).
 
• Bholanath Singh played an instrumental role in organizing the tribal resistance to safeguard their **autonomy and traditional rights over their lands**.
 
• The Tamar Revolt is considered one of the prominent tribal uprisings against colonial oppression in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tribal Uprisings in India:**

 
 
• Tribal revolts like the Tamar Revolt were often fueled by the British policies of land revenue, deforestation, and interference in traditional tribal practices.
 
• Other notable tribal uprisings include the **Santhal Revolt (1855-56)**, led by Sidhu and Kanhu, and the **Munda Rebellion (1899-1900)**, led by Birsa Munda.
 
 
 
• **Causes of Tribal Revolts:**
 
 
• Imposition of land taxes and seizure of tribal lands by colonial authorities.
 
• Exploitation by zamindars, moneylenders, and traders in tribal regions.
 
• Suppression of tribal customs, religious practices, and community autonomy.
 
 
 
• **British Revenue Policies:**
 
 
• The Permanent Settlement system introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 often favored landlords and left the tribal population vulnerable to exploitation.
 
• Shifting cultivation, a traditional practice of many tribal groups, was curtailed under British forest policies.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Tribal Revolts:**
 
 
• These uprisings highlighted the resistance of tribal communities to colonial exploitation and the need to address their grievances.
 
• Many tribal revolts were brutally suppressed, but they inspired later nationalist movements and reforms in tribal policies.
